research_notes: Initial research 2026-10-01: frozen roster, indexed parliamentary biography, recovered first-party 2013 biography and ABC 2008 profile, current party biography and targeted historical staff/employer searches. Frozen roster unchanged.

Archived personal biography establishes work across finance, transport and manufacturing, but no legal employer names, dates, leave or full-time evidence. Industry labels cannot resolve government control. Totals remain unknown, not zero.

Wikipedia repeats a detailed adviser chronology that is not in the ABC archival page cited for it. Aulich 1984–92, Field 1992–95, Murphy 1995–98 and Lennon to 2005 remain specifically attributed follow-up leads. Personal and ABC accounts describe two senators in the 1980s instead; resolve the discrepancy with contemporary staff records.

First speech identified as 11 August 2005 at 5:23pm, Hansard p108 onward. https://www.aph.gov.au/binaries/hansard/senate/dailys/ds110805.pdf returned 403 and later robots-blocked non-retryable; full text not obtained. Search result Birchalls/banking/early-childhood career belongs to Jess Greene, not Polley, and was excluded. UK Barclays LinkedIn namesake not matched or used.

Live former personal biography returned 502 Bad Gateway, recovered through public archived page. Live old ABC link redirects to homepage; archived profile retrieved successfully. These source errors did not stop research.

Follow up accessible first-speech transcript, 2003 ministerial staff listing, contemporary Field office and senator staff records; seek earlier finance/transport/manufacturing employers, substantive hours, employment breaks and study overlap. Broad profile searches exhausted for this initial pass; names needed for targeted employer annual reports.

Follow-up2026-10-02(non-material): targeted2005first-speech text, TerryAulich/ShayneMurphy office history,2003ministerial staff listing and earlier manufacturing/finance/transport employment. APH-targeted search returned Blocked by robots.txt, non-retryable; no retry. Searches on Tasmanian parliamentary/DPAC domains did not surface the contemporary staff listing. TasmanianTimes2006entry repeats existing Northern adviser lead, not new primary proof.

Exact chronology results were Wikipedia mirrors, factsnippet and an unsourced contact-directory biography; excluded as independent corroboration. No new employer identity, term, full-time evidence or employment break resolved. Preserve sourced facts and uncertainties. Next follow-up requires accessible first speech or contemporary staff-list archive; defer repetitive broad searches until a new lead is available.

Follow-up2026-10-04: a public first-person account by Paul Mallett, briefly employed in Senator Shayne Murphy's Launceston office in May1997, identifies Polley as the office's electorate officer. This materially resolves one senator and role at one observation month, but does not prove the Wikipedia1995–98 tenure, hours or leave. The other senator remains unresolved; the broad archived biography's reference to two senators in the1980s conflicts with the1997 observation and is preserved rather than rewritten.
